subject: Micro-segmentation landing zone & PV lifecycle runbook
messages:
From: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv@graycore.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private K8s landing zone for GrayCore - discovery

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this — GrayCore wants a private, on-prem Kubernetes landing zone to host our inference workloads (mostly customer-facing realtime pipelines + nightly batch retrains). High-level asks from our SRE/Platform owners: 
- 3 customer namespaces with strict network micro-segmentation,
- GPU pools for realtime model inference (NVIDIA A100 + some T4 for burst),
- Persistent volumes for model artifacts (high-throughput reads) and metadata DBs,
- An ephemeral NVMe cache layer for local model hot swaps,
- Block-level backups + point-in-time restore for critical volumes,
- Integration with our on-prem KMS and audit log pipeline.

We can share a short spreadsheet with IO/throughput targets and retention rules (attached). Can we do a short discovery call to align on constraints (rack topology, SAN vs NAS, VLAN design, and operational handoff)?

Attachments: GrayCore_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Thanks,
Rajiv
GrayCore Analytics — Platform Lead
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv@graycore.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private K8s landing zone for GrayCore - discovery

Hi Rajiv —

Appreciate the detail. I skimmed the requirements and we can definitely support the pattern you described. Proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Workshop (1.5h) to finalize constraints: rack-to-rack network, SAN vs local NVMe topology, and security/compliance (KMS + audit ingestion).
2) Landing-zone proposal:
  - Cluster sizing: 3 control-plane (HA), build two node pools initially: inference-gpu (pinned A100/T4, tainted), worker-standard (mix of 32–64GB machines for apps).
  - Storage plan: two primary classes — block-fast (iSCSI/FC backed, reclaimPolicy: Retain for DB/model-store) and ephemeral-nvme (LocalStorageClass for cache with local-provisioner).
  - Data protection: CSI snapshots + scheduled backups to on-prem object store; nightly incremental + weekly full; PV snapshot TTL 30d.
  - Networking: Calico with BPF mode, microsegmentation via NetworkPolicies + dedicated service CIDR per tenant; egress via NAT gateway pair with BGP for resilience.
  - Ops: document runbook for PV recovery, CSI driver validation, and an incident play for model rollback.

I attached an initial draft (20270721-graycore-landingzone-draft.pdf) and a storage-class matrix. Can your team do the workshop Friday 07/23 at 09:00 PT? If that works I’ll pull in engineering and storage SME.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachment: 20270721-graycore-landingzone-draft.pdf; pv-storage-class-matrix.xlsx
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private K8s landing zone for GrayCore - discovery

Team — forwarding GrayCore notes and our draft. Key context: customer runs a SAN (NetApp) in two racks and also has local NVMe on inference hosts for caching. They want fast read for model artifacts and durable backing for DBs.

Primary asks I want us to resolve before the Friday workshop:
- Storage recommendation: Rook/Ceph vs using NetApp CSI (their ops prefer vendor-backed storage). Evaluate recovery time and operational overhead.
- PV lifecycle: for model-store volumes we should use reclaimPolicy=Retain and snapshot schedule; for application ephemeral volumes use Delete. Confirm snapshot TTL and retention cadence.
- Node pools and autoscaling: inference-gpu pool must be pre-warmed and have a burst pool that can be scheduled across racks; suggest node-allocator with taints/tolerations + cluster-autoscaler with scale-down disabled for GPU baseline.
- Network: propose Calico in BPF mode, policy enforcement at namespace + pod level; egress via pair of NAT gateways with BGP to their core. Need to confirm whether their switches support EVPN/VXLAN if we propose overlay.
- Security: KMS integration for disk encryption, TLS mutual auth for CSI, and audit log forwarding to customer syslog endpoint.

Please review inline below and reply with blockers. Jordan — can you run a quick tech check on NetApp CSI compatibility vs Rook for our CSI snapshot strategy? Karthik — I’ll need your input on cluster sizing (control-plane SLOs) and autoscaler knobs. Marissa — I’d like your ops readiness checklist (recovery, runbooks, oncall handoff).

Forwarded message reproduced below for reference.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Private K8s landing zone for GrayCore - discovery

Neha — good summary. A few inline thoughts / concerns: 

> - Storage recommendation: Rook/Ceph vs using NetApp CSI (their ops prefer vendor-backed storage). Evaluate recovery time and operational overhead.

If GrayCore ops prefer NetApp, we should lean that way unless their NetApp is too old. Rook brings flexibility but adds an ops burden (mon/osd placement, quorum). Proposal: primary PVs on NetApp with NetApp CSI; offer Rook as fallback only if NetApp can't provide required IOPS/latency. Document runbook for OSD failure and OSD replacement if we recommend Rook.

> - PV lifecycle: for model-store volumes we should use reclaimPolicy=Retain and snapshot schedule; for application ephemeral volumes use Delete. Confirm snapshot TTL and retention cadence.

Agree. Add: for model-store, set volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer and storage class with allowVolumeExpansion=true. Provide an emergency detach/reattach procedure (steps + validation). For critical DBs, set fsType xfs and mountOptions to avoid small-file penalty.

> - Node pools and autoscaling: inference-gpu pool must be pre-warmed and have a burst pool that can be scheduled across racks; suggest node-allocator with taints/tolerations + cluster-autoscaler with scale-down disabled for GPU baseline.

We should recommend a small baseline of always-on GPU nodes equal to their typical concurrency (from spreadsheet). Burst pool can be spot/cheap T4 nodes but only if the customer is ok with preemption. Also: enforce PodDisruptionBudgets for model-serving deployments and use guaranteed QoS for critical pods.

Operational asks: we need a PV recovery runbook and a storage-validation playbook (iops/latency tests, snapshot restore tests). Jordan — can you take the storage-validation checklist? Karthik — can you produce a control-plane SLO doc (etcd restore steps + etcd snapshot frequency).

Marissa
Director, Customer Ops — Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv@graycore.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private K8s landing zone for GrayCore - discovery 

Thanks all — quick summary and actions after internal reviews: 

Agreed decisions:
- Use NetApp CSI as primary storage for durable model-store + DB PVs (reclaimPolicy=Retain).
- Local NVMe will be used for ephemeral model-cache; implement a LocalStorageClass with node-affinity to inference hosts.
- CSI snapshots: hourly incremental snapshots for DBs (retain 7d), daily snapshots for model-store (retain 30d).
- GPU pools: baseline always-on nodes (customer to confirm baseline counts); separate burst pool of preemptible T4 nodes. Cluster-autoscaler: disable scale-down for baseline GPU nodes.
- Networking: Calico (BPF), namespace-level policies, egress via dual NAT with BGP.
- Security: integrate with customer KMS, forward audit logs to their syslog endpoint, and enforce TLS on CSI control-plane.

Action owners / next steps:
- Jordan Blake: storage validation and NetApp CSI compatibility testing (due 2027-07-28). Attachment: pv-storage-class-matrix.xlsx.
- Karthik Iyer: control-plane SLO doc, etcd snapshot cadence and restore play (due 2027-07-27).
- Marissa Cole: PV recovery runbook + ops checklist for go-live (due 2027-07-26).
- Neha (me): consolidate runbook draft and host Friday workshop 07/23 09:00 PT. Runbook draft attached (neha-runbook-diff.patch + 20270721-graycore-landingzone-draft.pdf).

Rajiv — please confirm the Friday slot and whether GrayCore is ok with NetApp as primary. If they need a Rook proof-of-concept instead, we can scope that as a follow-up.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
